Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Komal Mehrotra
Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri S.N. Srivastava, learned Advocate appearing for
the respondent No. 3.
It is admitted fact of the matter that the land belonging to the petitioners had been acquired by the acquisition notifications in the year 2004 under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
It is also an admitted fact that the petitioners had received compensation in terms of the award prepared by the competent authority.
Only this much is sought to be submitted in the writ petition that only paper possession has been taken by the State Government and the actual physical has not been handed over to the acquiring body.

sentences.text:
The submission, thus, is that the provisions of Section 24 (2) of the Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short 'the Act,
2013') are attracted in the facts of the present case and the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation under the Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
We find inherent fallacy in the argument of the learned counsel for the petitioners, inasmuch as,
under the Land Acquisition Act' 1894, there is no concept of transfer on paper possession.

The Apex Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal & ors etc.; 2020 (8) SCC 129 had considered this aspect of the matter and has held that the Land Acquisition Act conceives transfer of physical possession by issuance of possession memo.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal & ors etc.; 2020 (8) SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the statement made in the instant writ petition, it is more than evident that the possession memo has been prepared for transfer of physical possession of the acquired land to the acquiring body.

With the issuance of the possession memo and declaration of the award, the land in question stood vested with the State Government in accordance with the provisions of Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act' 1894.

Divesting after the declaration of the award and taking possession by preparation of possession memo is not permissible within the meaning of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894.

Even otherwise, the provisions of Section 24(2) of the Act' 2013 are not attracted in a case where compensation under the award has been received by the tenure holders and delivery of possession by possession memo has been made.

In view of the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs.
Manoharlal & ors (supra), no direction, as such, can be given to entertain the representation moved by the petitioners.

sentences.text: The writ petition is dismissed as misconceived.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Apex Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal & ors etc.; 2020 (8) SCC 129 had considered this aspect of the matter and has held that the Land Acquisition Act conceives transfer of physical possession by issuance of possession memo.

1894.
Even otherwise, the provisions of Section 24(2) of the Act' 2013 are not attracted in a case where compensation under the award has been received by the tenure holders and delivery of possession by possession memo has been made.
